description: Committee recommends dry storm pond in Cahill Park.

Construction planned for 2025/2026.
Funded by $2.2 million from stormwater utility reserve.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against

Residents expressed concerns about the dry pond's size and safety.
Staff promised the dry pond would drain within 24 hours of a storm.

description: City advances capital plan for natural and green spaces.
Plan includes bird-friendly building guidelines and dark sky initiatives.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Councillor Davies clarified the $6 million funding is for capital, not directly mill rate.
Migratory songbirds are federally protected and affected by window strikes.

Natural areas provide storm water management, flood prevention, and carbon storage.

speakers.name: Jan Shadick
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Natural and Naturalized Areas
said: Allocate funds for bird-friendly building guidelines in the budget.
New bird-friendly buildings would save thousands of birds from window strikes.
City Hall is a bird strike hotspot; prioritize deterrent markers.

description: The report highlighted 25,000+ incidents and new programs.
City spent $45,000 net for paramedic overtime in 2024.

chips.text: Chief Wegren explained using overtime for paramedics due to short-term provincial funding.
Residents near the EWC and downtown temporary shelter receive bylaw support.

description: Fire Department equipment repairs average 41 days.
Its 1964 shop is too small for the growing fleet.
New maintenance shop requested in 2026-2027 budget.

chips.text: Councillor Keller questioned the financial impact of delayed maintenance.
Firefighters experience training delays due to equipment unavailability.
The financial cost of not doing regular maintenance is currently unknown.
An asset manager will track costs and identify end-of-life for equipment.

description: Opioid overdose incidents in Saskatoon have doubled, straining emergency services.
City leaders advocate for better provincial data and resources.
Frontline workers overwhelmed, urge city leadership and better healthcare access.

chips.text: Mayor Block questioned why supports are incremental, expecting different results.
No clear solutions offered for preventing repeat overdoses or street interventions.
Indigenous people, unhoused youth, and children are disproportionately affected by the crisis.

speakers.name: Toby Esterby
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Saskatoon Opioid Poisoning Crisis
said: Applauds Fire Department for saving hundreds of lives in the crisis.
Urges city to lead in solving systemic problems, not just apply band-aids.
Advocates for opening healthcare access; emergency rooms are turning people away.

speakers.name: Connor Rodriguez
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Saskatoon Opioid Poisoning Crisis
said: Highlights high addiction rates, linking them to colonial history and unhoused Indigenous youth.
Shares youth's plea for funded safe consumption sites and valuing frontline workers.
Calls for action, preventative measures, and wrap-around services for vulnerable youth.

speakers.name: Kayla DwMong
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: PHR - Saskatoon Opioid Poisoning Crisis
said: Staff are exhausted; Prairie Harm Reduction closed due to grief and relentless overdoses.
More lives lost in 3 months than all last year; current approaches are failing.
Criticizes city council for not showing up or meeting with affected people.
